posts: Two numbers from the same World Bank survey. 1.3 billion adults have no financial account. 86% of adults own a mobile phone. Put those side by side and the usual explanation falls apart 🧵

1/ Whatever is keeping a billion people out of the financial system, it isn't that they lack a device — and it hasn't been for years. The honest answer is less comfortable than a technology gap. It's arithmetic.

2/ A bank account costs a fixed amount to open and run. Identity verification, compliance, servicing. Those costs don't shrink with the balance — verifying a customer with $40 costs about what it costs to verify one with $40,000.
3/ So below a certain balance every account is a small recurring loss. Nobody is excluded out of malice. They're excluded by a spreadsheet.
4/ Mobile money moved that threshold down a lot. But it moved the threshold — it didn't remove it. There's still an institution deciding if you clear a bar, still a counterparty holding the balance.

5/ A self-custodial wallet is a keypair. Issuing one more costs ~nothing, needs nobody's approval, has no minimum. The economics that excluded a billion people stop applying. Whether the result is USEFUL is a separate question.

6/ And for most of crypto's history the honest answer was "not very." Telling someone on an uncertain income they can hold something that might fall 40% in a month isn't inclusion. It's a different exclusion with better branding.

7/ That's what tokenization changed. Stablecoins put dollars in the wallet. Ondo's USDY (~$2.1B) puts short-term Treasuries in it. PAX Gold puts one troy ounce of allocated LBMA gold in it. Ondo's stock products span 440+ US equities and ETFs.
8/ So the pitch stops being "hold this volatile asset" and becomes "hold the same things wealthy people hold to store value — dollars, Treasuries, gold — in an account nobody had to approve."
9/ It's already happening without permission: ~$33T of stablecoin transfers settled on public chains in 2025, +72% y/y, and 71% of LatAm firms use them for cross-border settlement.

10/ Honestly, what a wallet still can't do: no credit, no recourse, no chargeback. And key loss is real — recovery design is the weakest part of this industry-wide. Any version of this argument that skips that is selling something. https://www.swopme.co/blog/banking-the-unbanked-self-custody
